description: The completion algebra's not/and/or over ground outcomes (research 0031 row 15, #3164). HAND-AUTHORED from research 0031's advice section 3 (the strong-Kleene tables, the scoped-absorption rule, and the closure implication table), never from an implementation's output. A leaf is an outcome: {arm: holds} | {arm: fails, false_code} | {arm: not_completed, kind, scope} (a fault has no scope) | {arm: limit_exceeded, limit}. Each case's `why` is printed by every replay with a failure of that case. An expression is {op: not|and|or, args: [...]}; and/or fold their args left to right. A non-completion is a STOP (capacity, work_cap and instantiation at any scope; host_refusal and reply_unreadable at request scope only) or a FAULT (inconsistent_theory, malformed_outcome), which carries no scope and ranks above a caller's limit (seat:caa's ruling on #3179). A case with `construct` names a kind and scope that must be REFUSED by each core's checked constructor (`refused: true`); its `expr` holds a hand-built value of that illegal pair, which a core that can form one (Go, TypeScript) must read as malformed_outcome, and which Rust cannot form at all. Every core replays it: the written order must give `expect` exactly, and every reordering of every and/or node's args must give an outcome of the same CLASS (holds, fails, absorbable undecided, dominant undecided), so a correct verdict never depends on evaluation order. Within a class the leftmost operand is reported, so the exact cause is order-dependent by design. A limit is an opaque name here: the layer that sets a limit owns its vocabulary, and the algebra only carries it.

cases.name: closure_body_holds_head_absent
cases.why: closure obligation Body => Head-in-table, as (not Body) or Head: a true body with its head absent is a definite violation

cases.name: closure_body_holds_head_present
cases.why: a true body with its head present satisfies the obligation

cases.name: closure_body_fails_head_absent
cases.why: a false body satisfies the obligation whether or not the head is present

cases.name: closure_body_undecided_head_absent
cases.why: an undecided body cannot conceal a missing head: closure is not established (the shape of the #3123 omission)

cases.name: closure_body_undecided_head_present
cases.why: a present head discharges the obligation even though the body is undecided

cases.name: closure_false_conjunct_absorbs_undecided_body_literal
cases.why: another body conjunct is independently false, so the body is false and the head need not be present

cases.name: closure_true_conjunct_keeps_undecided_body_literal
cases.why: H and U is U, so the body is undecided and an absent head stays not established

cases.name: closure_negated_undecided_literal
cases.why: a body \+ q with q undecided: not(U) = U, so the rule neither fires nor is shown unable to fire

cases.name: closure_request_stop_not_absorbed_by_present_head

cases.name: and_fault_then_limit_reports_fault

cases.name: or_holds_keeps_fault

cases.name: and_two_faults_reports_first

cases.name: closure_fault_not_discharged_by_present_head
cases.why: a present head does not discharge a fault

cases.name: fault_at_literal_scope_is_refused
cases.why: a fault with a chosen local scope would be absorbed into an answer, so it cannot be constructed, and a hand-built one reads as malformed

cases.name: malformed_outcome_at_request_scope_is_refused
cases.why: a fault carries no scope at all, not even the widest
